comments.author: Alex Kim
comments.body: Security review signed off; retested with dual-tab manual flow—second submit now gets 410.

content.text: Security review signed off; retested with dual-tab manual flow—second submit now gets 410.
A password-reset link can be consumed twice if two browser tabs both POST the new password within about one second of each other. Both responses return 200 and establish sessions.
Tokens must be single-use: the first successful redemption should invalidate the token atomically so a concurrent attempt receives 410 Gone with “link already used”.

Race is reproducible with two tabs sharing the same token query param. Both hit POST /auth/reset-password before either transaction commits the used_at column. Leading theory is missing SELECT … FOR UPDATE (or an equivalent single-flight Redis lock on token_hash) around the redeem path; the unique partial index on unused tokens is not enough under read-committed isolation.
If a reset email leaks, an attacker and the legitimate user can both set passwords; audit logs show two password_changed events for one token_id.
